name: download-owned
title: Download an owned asset
summary: Download an owned Unreal Engine asset's files to a folder, choosing the engine version when there are several

inputs.name: Uid
inputs.description: Listing UID of an owned asset

inputs.name: Dir
inputs.description: Folder to download into (created if missing)

steps.why: Find the asset in the library and download every file, hash-checked
steps.check: ok is true; file_hashes_verified; sidecar .fabcli-asset.json in the folder

on_error.ambiguous_artifact: The listing has several engine versions or platforms: show error.available to the user, then re-run with --engine UE_X.Y (and --platform) from it
on_error.not_owned: Not in the library: if it is free, claim it (fabcli claim <uid>) and retry; otherwise the user buys it on Fab
on_error.output_collision: Files already exist (error.conflicts): pick another folder, or add --force if the user agrees to overwrite

notes: Set FABCLI_LIBRARY_CACHE=1 first: the UID form reads the library, which takes about 100 s per 1,000 assets when not cached.
Large assets take a while; progress is on stderr. The command exits when its JSON is written.
Only Unreal Engine formats can be downloaded. Importing into a project is a separate step.
